title: In vitro protocol for the optimal induction of inflammation in human monocyte cell lines
protocol: Remove 96-well plate of differentiated THP-1 cells from the incubator.
Examine cells under a microscope.
Ensure that cells are alive and sufficient in number before subsequent steps.
Treat the cells with LPS at a concentration of 100 ng/mL.
Add LPS in RPMI media to the wells for the 5 h time point.
Incubate plate until the next time point.
Repeat addition of LPS-laden media for subsequent time points as they are reached.
Remove contents of the wells using a multi-channel pipette at 5 h post addition of LPS.
Wash each well once with PBS.
Add 100 μL of 4% PFA to each well using a multi-channel pipette.
Pour an aliquot of the 4% PFA solution into a reagent reservoir well.
Add PFA to each row/column using a multi-channel pipette based on the number of channels available.
Incubate plate at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 10 minutes.
Wash plate wells gently with PBS using a multi-channel pipette.
Collect and dispose of PFA waste in the correct waste stream.
Add 100 μL of 0.1% Triton X-100 to each well.
Incubate plate at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 10 minutes.
Remove contents of the plate using a multi-channel pipette and wash once with PBS.
Add 100 μL of 0.1% BSA to each well.
Incubate plate at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 10 minutes.
Prepare a fresh dilution of primary antibodies during incubation time.
Stain the plate for four proteins: p-IκBα, IκBα, p-p65, and p65.
Be gentle when washing the plate wells with PBS.
Set aside one well in the control column for each secondary antibody used.
Add an IgG antibody control to each reserved well.
Remove contents of the plate using a multi-channel pipette.
Add 100 μL of primary antibody per well.
Incubate plate at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 1 h.
Make a fresh dilution of secondary antibodies with the ratio 0.6 μL antibody/1 mL of 0.1% BSA.
Add one drop of NucBlue Fixed Cell ReadyProbes Reagent per 1 mL of 0.1% BSA when making the secondary antibody stocks.
Turn the light off in the fume hood.
Remove contents of the plate using a multi-channel pipette.
Add 100 μL of secondary antibody per well.
Cover plate with aluminum foil.
Leave plate in the dark for 1 hour at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Remove contents of the plate using a multi-channel pipette.
Wash plate twice with PBS.
Add 100 μL of PBS/well.
Look through the eyepieces and manually focus the first IgG antibody control well onto the DAPI stain using the 408 channel.
Close the shutter and proceed to Smart Setup on the Zen software.
Add the DAPI and 647 fluorophores into the program and click on the “Best Signal” setting.
Set the pinhole size to 1 Airy Unit (AU).
Optimize the settings for the DAPI signal.
Checkmark the DAPI channel and click “live scan”.
Find an area of the field with a few, bright, well-spaced cells.
Use the joystick to shift the field and refocus as needed.
Increase the digital offset by one unit at a time until blue pixels in the background are gone.
Switch to Histo display mode.
Draw a region around the brightest cell in the field of view in the graphics tab.
Adjust Gain (Master) until the brightest pixels in the histogram are between 2000–2500.
Increase Gain (Master) and Laser Power until the DAPI stain is clearly visible.
Ensure the Gain (Master) value is between 450–850.
Monitor Mean intensity value to prevent sample bleaching.
Continue adjusting settings until image quality improves consistently.
Repeat steps for the 647-fluorophore channel once satisfied with DAPI stain quality.
Adjust settings for IgG antibody control until red pixels are just barely visible.
Set Acquisition Mode averaging number = 4 and speed = max value.
Proceed to automate the confocal microscope to image each of the 96 wells.
Click on the tile scan option in the left button set.
Focus manually on the DAPI channel until cells are clearly seen for each well.
Click on the add tile position button present in the tile scan dialog box to store x, y, and z parameters of the well.
Repeat focusing and adding tile positions for every well of the 96-well plate.
Observe trends in 647 intensities with the following proteins (p-IκBα, IκBα, p-p65, and p65) across time points using the grid feature of Zen.
Monitor changes in protein levels for p-IκBα as they increase over time.
Record initial decrease followed by an increase in IκBα levels.
Track increases in p-p65 levels with time.
Note translocation to the nucleus rather than overall change for p65.
Passage a new 96-well plate of THP-1 cells and remove from the incubator once ready.
Create a plate layout to test the efficacy of a compound in suppressing inflammation induced by LPS using the following guidelines.
Perform each variation in triplicate, resulting in 32 unique combinations.
Observe the effect of anti-inflammatory on levels of p-IκBα, IκBα, p-p65, and p65 with 8 unique combinations per protein studied.
Include a control without LPS and a positive control with LPS only for each protocol.
Test six therapeutic combinations alongside prophylactic PBA, simultaneous addition of PBA with LPS, and therapeutic dosing of PBA.
Study increasing concentrations of PBA to observe dose-dependent effects on the four protein markers at optimized time points.
Prepare a plate layout to test the synergistic effects of PBA and DEX on suppressing inflammation induced by LPS.
Use an 8x8 grid with 2-fold dilutions of each drug.
Test 8 concentrations of PBA including no drug added, starting from the highest concentration desired.
Test 8 concentrations of DEX including no drug added, starting from the highest concentration desired.
Create a stock solution for DEX at 400 μM.
Add 100 μL of the 8x DEX to each well in the first row.
Perform 2-fold dilutions using a multi-channel pipette for the next 6 rows, omitting the 8th row.
Prepare a 160 mM solution of PBA.
Prepare a 320 mM solution of PBA.
Add 100 μL of the 16x PBA to the first well in the first column.
Add 100 μL of the 8x PBA to wells 2–8 in the first column.
Perform 2-fold dilutions using a multi-channel pipette for the next 6 rows, omitting the 8th row.
Add 100 μL of 4x LPS (400 ng/mL) to all 96 wells.
Incubate the plate for the length of time needed for optimal induction of p-IκBα or p-p65.
